correctness.rationale: For unequal exponents the shorter input is a factor of the longer. For equal exponents, the two common overlap factors generate the whole common-subsequence downset: a common word absent from the first overlap necessarily starts and ends with an A-alphabet symbol, hence embeds in the second overlap by disjointness. A-symbol and B-symbol multiplicities respectively force the two overlaps to be incomparable. This proves the one/two classification for all nonempty disjoint-alphabet words and positive exponents. The actual packaged standalone checker verifies 1,144 finite instances and 92,735 common words; these tests support rather than replace the proof.

value.rationale: A complete natural infinite-family classification of an inclusion-maximal string-alignment invariant, covering arbitrary internal symbol repetitions and all two-power parameters. It exhibits a common-subsequence language generated by only two maximal words and an arbitrarily large shortest-maximal versus longest gap even on a binary alphabet, giving an exact benchmark distinct from general MCS algorithms.
